reason: Title explicitly names PRPH2/RDS gene mutations and describes phenotypic variability in patients. Directly on-topic for PRPH2 (peripherin/RDS). Thin abstract does not reduce confidence given unambiguous title.
Abstract centers entirely on PRPH2 variants causing macular dystrophies. Peripherin-2 protein function and pathogenic variant spectrum are the subject of the paper. Squarely on-topic for PRPH2.

Abstract reports Y141C mutation in the peripherin/RDS gene (PRPH2) causing pattern dystrophy with high intrafamilial variability, plus anti-VEGF treatment of associated CNV. Directly about PRPH2 disease genetics and management.

Title unambiguously reports autosomal dominant central areolar choroidal dystrophy caused by a codon-142 mutation in the Peripherin/RDS gene (PRPH2). No abstract, but the title alone establishes direct relevance.

Abstract fully characterises recessive bi-allelic PRPH2 mutations causing a distinct Leber congenital amaurosis phenotype in children and prominent maculopathy in adults, with asymptomatic heterozygous parents showing macular signs. Core PRPH2 genotype-phenotype literature.
Abstract identifies a PRPH2 mutation in the diagnostic workup of presumed autoimmune retinopathy, extends the PRPH2 phenotypic spectrum, and reports intravitreal steroid response. On-topic for PRPH2.

Review of autosomal optic atrophy genes linked to mitochondrial dysfunction. ACO2 (aconitase 2, mitochondrial) is a known causative gene for autosomal optic atrophy with retinal involvement. The review covers all currently identified causative genes in this category, making it directly relevant to ACO2.

Genotyping study of a Northern European Joubert syndrome cohort. CC2D2A (JBTS9) and RPGRIP1L (JBTS7/MKS5) are among the most frequently mutated Joubert syndrome genes; this cohort study would report mutations in both. Title and keywords align tightly.

Review of mechanotransduction in auditory and vestibular hair cells. CDH23 and PCDH15 encode the two subunits of the tip link that gates mechanotransduction channels — they are the central molecules of this process. CIB2 modulates TMC-channel-based mechanotransduction. A review of hair-cell mechanotransduction molecules would cover all three in depth.

Investigates ATP effects on gamma-S-crystallin (the CRYGS protein) stability in the human eye lens under crowding conditions. Directly studies the biophysics of the CRYGS-encoded protein. Relevant to cataract mechanism.

Studies the G57W variant of human gamma-S-crystallin (CRYGS) using hydrogen-deuterium exchange, characterising pro-cataractogenic conformational excursions. CRYGS G57W is a known pathogenic mutation. Directly relevant to CRYGS.

Abstract directly studies PCDH15 (protocadherin 15) dimer nanomechanics under physiological Ca2+ and characterises the V507D point mutation associated with non-syndromic hearing loss. Squarely on-topic for PCDH15.

Biophysical mutagenesis study of the whirlin (WHRN) PDZ tandem, mapping residue-level energetics of transient misfolding. Whirlin is the scaffold protein encoded by WHRN, mutations in which cause Usher syndrome 2D (retinal dystrophy plus deafness). A structural study of the disease protein is within scope for a gene-focused ophthalmogenetics library.

Identifies a BBS1 splice-donor mutation causing an exceptionally mild Bardet-Biedl phenotype and demonstrates U1 snRNA gene therapy restoring correct BBS1 splicing in patient fibroblasts. Directly about BBS1 genetics and therapeutic correction.

Title reports novel photoreceptor guanylate cyclase functions revealed by targeted deletion; GUCY2D encodes retinal guanylate cyclase 1 (RetGC-1/RETGC-1), GUCA1A encodes its activator GCAP1. Both genes are directly studied. Missing abstract does not reduce confidence given the unambiguous title.

Review of membrane-bound guanylyl cyclases localised to the ciliary compartment. GUCY2D (RetGC-1) is the canonical cilium-restricted retinal membrane GC; RD3 is a regulator of RetGC trafficking/activity. The abstract specifically covers cilium-restricted receptor-type GCs, placing GUCY2D and RD3 at the centre of the review.

Microarray expression profiling of the rd3 mouse retina specifically to characterise the RD3 gene-deficiency phenotype (LCA12 model). Identifies phototransduction and immune-response pathway changes. Directly studies RD3 function and pathomechanism.

Hearing loss paper proposing the RBF/DnJ mouse as an animal model of Usher syndrome type IIa. Usher IIa is caused by USH2A mutations, not RD3. The paper was likely co-cited with RD3 literature due to the shared hearing-plus-retinal phenotype angle, but the primary scientific focus is on hearing loss and Usher IIa pathology, not on RD3 gene function or retinal disease. Without an abstract the connection to RD3 cannot be confirmed, and the title alone suggests USH2A biology rather than RD3.

Biochemical characterisation of hierarchical protein interactions with U4/U6 snRNA and a defined biochemical role for U4/U6 proteins. PRPF3 (hPrp3/RP18) is a U4/U6 snRNP protein; SNRNP200 (Brr2) is a U4/U5/U6 tri-snRNP helicase; RNU4ATAC encodes U4atac snRNA of the minor spliceosome. This paper addresses the molecular interactions at the heart of all three gene products.

Review of mRNA metabolism defects in neuronal disease, covering retinitis pigmentosa as a major example alongside SMA and XLMR. PRPF3 (RP18) mutations cause RP through mRNA splicing defects. The paper explicitly discusses how pre-mRNA processing mutations cause tissue-specific retinal degeneration, placing PRPF3-related RP at its centre.
